chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The cursing (li'an) does not occur until he claims that he has seen it.

key_terms.اللِّعَانُ: Li'an, the ritual of mutual cursing between a husband and wife regarding adultery
key_terms.عَايَنَ: He witnessed, implying direct personal observation

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of Li'an in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a critical evidentiary prerequisite for Li'an, requiring the husband to assert direct visual observation (mu'ayana) of the illicit act rather than mere hearsay. This condition underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on the reliability of personal testimony in the solemn oath-cursing procedure, distinguishing it from general witness requirements in other legal contexts.
